items.title: [aljazeera.com] Six-day Ukraine-Russia truce ends as emergency apps are hacked
items.content_html: A six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region ended late Nov. 1 after Moscow declined Kyiv’s offer to extend it, Ukrainian officials said. The pause, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and with the involvement of Pope Leo XIV, enabled humanitarian deliveries and evacuations. Neither side reported violations during the truce. Within hours of the truce’s end, Ukraine said its nationwide air-raid alert app had been compromised and briefly sent false warnings of radiation, nuclear and chemical threats, street fighting and Russia’s Oreshnik missile. Ukraine’s Air Force said there was no radiation threat, and the Ukrainian strategic communications center blamed Russia for the hack. Russia later said its emergencies app had suffered a “massive cyberattack” that spread false information but did not identify a perpetrator. It was unclear whether the two incidents were connected. Fighting continued elsewhere: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian attacks had left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian households without power. He offered to stop Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries if Washington supplied Patriot interceptor missiles. U.S.-mediated talks are expected to resume in November after stalling following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

items.title: [theguardian.com] France protests draw 320,000 as clashes spread to German cities
items.content_html: About 320,000 people protested across France on Saturday, Oct. 31, in a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs, education and public services; youth groups put turnout closer to 500,000. Most marches were peaceful, but clashes broke out as crowds dispersed in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Toulouse. Police used tear gas, water cannon and baton charges, and authorities reported more than 560 arrests nationwide. A Molotov cocktail struck a police officer in Paris in what Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called attempted murder. The movement began with students protesting poor school conditions, teacher shortages and university admissions they say disadvantage poorer applicants, then drew unions and Yellow Vest activists. The government’s turnout estimate fell from 410,000 the previous weekend and 550,000 on Oct. 17, when riots and looting damaged shops and public buildings. Student organizations have called for school and university blockades, while a general strike is expected in the coming days. The GenZ regelt! campaign also organized youth-led protests in 34 German cities over living costs, education funding and compulsory military service. After largely peaceful daytime marches, violence erupted in Frankfurt, where shops were looted and a gun store was among those targeted. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. Police also used water cannon or pepper spray in several cities.

items.title: [reuters.com] Russia's independent Novaya Gazeta to close Nov. 9 under pressure
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s last independent newspapers still operating inside the country, says it will end operations on Nov. 9 after losing access to its Moscow office and reader-donation system. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said Russian authorities and security services had forced the newsroom to stop working. The paper plans to publish a final issue. The closure follows years of restrictions that intensified after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Authorities revoked the paper’s media licence, blocked its website and designated it a “foreign agent” in September 2026. This month, police searched Sokolov’s home, and investigative reporter Oleg Roldugin was arrested in a criminal case. Novaya Gazeta says the loss of its premises and funding left it unable to continue. Its separately operated sister publication, Novaya Gazeta Europe, will keep publishing from abroad. Founded in 1993, the newspaper became known for investigations into corruption and human-rights abuses. Six of its journalists and contributors were killed, including Anna Politkovskaya, who reported on the Chechen wars.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from? Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch. Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.

items.title: [theguardian.com] China expels 33 senior officials as Xi tightens party discipline
items.content_html: China’s ruling Communist Party expelled 33 senior officials at the close of a four-day leadership meeting in Beijing on Oct. 29, confirming the removal of former senior military commander Zhang Youxia, former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and others. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military. The party’s communiqué cited serious disciplinary and legal violations without detailing individual allegations. Only 279 of the 376 full and alternate Central Committee members appointed in 2022 attended — the lowest attendance at a plenum under President Xi Jinping, with a record number of empty seats. Purges have reduced the seven-member Central Military Commission, which commands China’s armed forces, to Xi and General Zhang Shengmin, a military anti-corruption official. The party promoted Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo at the meeting. The meeting focused on internal discipline and anti-corruption, while analysts differ on whether the drive chiefly addresses graft or reinforces Xi’s authority. The party also confirmed that its 21st congress will take place in Beijing in the second half of 2027, when it will reshuffle its leadership and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term.

items.title: [nytimes.com] Venezuelan opposition leader returns, presses for 2027 presidential vote
items.content_html: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Caracas after nearly 10 months in exile and said Thursday that presidential elections should be held in 2027, citing a transition plan outlined by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. She said her own team, not a government, arranged her return and thanked President Donald Trump’s administration for capturing former President Nicolás Maduro in January. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez also said elections would be held but set no date. She said they would follow reforms and be organized by a renewed electoral authority. Machado said she had received no message from Rodríguez and is not part of Washington-backed talks between the government and opposition factions, though she wants the talks to succeed. Machado’s party is excluded from the talks, which are addressing changes to the Supreme Court and electoral council. U.S. officials have said Rodríguez should leave office in 2027 after those reforms. Machado also criticized a U.S.-Venezuela oil agreement for lacking transparency.

items.title: [euronews.com] Lagarde exit opens ECB succession as French borrowing costs rise
items.content_html: European Central Bank policymakers held the deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct. 29, but President Christine Lagarde said they had seriously discussed a rate increase as energy prices and bond yields tightened financing conditions for households and businesses. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, and average 10-year government bond yields had risen about 35 basis points since the ECB’s September forecast. France’s 10-year borrowing cost topped 5% last week for the first time since 2002. The same day, Lagarde said she would leave the Frankfurt-based central bank on Feb. 7, 2027, before the end of her eight-year term, saying she wanted to speak on issues beyond monetary policy. Her departure opens a contest to lead the institution that sets interest rates across the euro area. Markets showed little reaction to the announcement, with analysts saying the ECB’s established practices were likely to outlast its president. Investors were pricing in three further rate increases by the end of 2027, which would bring the deposit rate to 3.25%. The ECB’s next policy meeting is scheduled for Dec. 17.
